cards.back: Loading everything that already exists, as opposed to live changes. Run at launch, when adding a source, after data corruption, and after changing parsing, chunking or the embedding model.
time = documents ÷ (per-connector rate × parallel connectors). 10M ÷ (50/s × 3) ≈ 18.5 h.
Live changes and backfill use different topics and consumer groups, so the backfill can be scaled, paused or throttled alone.
A token bucket per source API keeps total calls under quota, with a reserved share for live updates.
First list every document ID into the backfill topic, saving the listing cursor after each page; then process them.
"Fetch latest, compare version, write if newer", so reprocessing after a crash is harmless.
Documents that keep failing are parked with the error and replayed after a fix, not retried forever.
Make every index write conditional: write only if the incoming version is newer. Partitioning by doc_id only helps within a lane.
Reconcile counts per source and space, spot-check documents end to end, and run the golden-set evals.
Build a new index beside the live one from stored parsed docs, dual-write live changes, compare evals, switch reads blue-green, keep the old index for rollback.
chunks × average tokens per chunk × price per token. 50M × 400 = 20B tokens.

quiz.q: 10M documents, 3 connectors at 50 docs/s each. Roughly how long is the backfill?
The slow backfill fetched v3 of a doc while a live edit already wrote v4. What prevents an overwrite?
choices: Conditional writes: only if the version is newer
quiz.why: Only the version check is safe across lanes.

quiz.q: A backfill worker crashes after three days. What makes resuming safe?
choices: A saved listing cursor, idempotent writes and committed offsets
quiz.why: Checkpoints plus idempotent processing make restarts harmless.

quiz.q: Which number must stay flat while a backfill runs?
quiz.why: The backfill must never starve live updates.

quiz.q: You change the embedding model. How should you rebuild?
choices: Re-embed in place in the live index
Build a new index alongside, compare evals, then switch reads
Pause the assistant for a day
quiz.why: Never re-index in place; switch blue-green with rollback.

quiz.q: Where should the re-index read documents from?
quiz.why: Rebuilding from stored copies means quotas don't matter.

quiz.q: A document keeps failing to parse. What should happen?
choices: Park it in a dead-letter queue and replay after a fix
quiz.why: A DLQ keeps the job moving and the failure visible.
